item.title: El día que la IA decidió trabajar en equipo (más JARVIS, menos Skynet) — Thu Nov 5, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto En los últimos meses hemos visto cómo la IA escribe código, genera imágenes o responde preguntas. Pero hay algo mucho más interesante ocurriendo: ¿qué pasa cuando varias IAs empiezan a trabajar juntas como un equipo real?
En esta sesión vamos a llevar esa idea a la práctica montando, desde cero, una factoría de software basada en agentes IA. Cada agente tendrá un rol claro —programador, QA, diseñador, incluso músico— y todos estarán coordinados por un agente orquestador (el “project manager” de toda la vida) que se encargará de repartir tareas, tomar decisiones y mantener el flujo de trabajo.
Lo interesante es que no será teoría: lo veremos en directo. Los agentes se comunicarán entre ellos, pasarán tareas y construirán algo real delante de nosotros. Sin guión y sin red, mostrando cómo funcionan de verdad estos sistemas cuando los pones a trabajar.

item.title: Author Talk: Robert Moor — Thu Nov 5, 2:00 PM — Toronto Botanical Garden
item.description:
To truly grasp the wisdom of a tree, you need to begin thinking like one… One day, years ago, Robert Moor set out to climb a tree near his home in British Columbia. This simple act unwittingly launched him on a decade-long adventure around the world, ranging from Papua to Tanzania. Along the way, he learned the art of “tree-thinking,” which, he discovered, has the power to break open some of humanity’s oldest questions: What is the secret to truly growing old? How do we set down roots in an increasingly chaotic world? Most importantly, how should we—as individuals, as communities, as stewards of the earth—live?
Moor’s mind-expanding talk, “How To Think Like A Tree” will reveal the myriad ways trees teach us to “grow wise.” The genius of trees, he argues, is that they deftly combine four entwined processes: branching, pruning, gnarling, and rooting. item.title: 🍂 Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat! 🍦 — Sun Nov 8, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! ## 🍂 **Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat!** 🍦
Toronto doesn’t have many true hiking trails — but Crothers Woods is one of the best! This beautiful wooded trail is especially stunning in the fall, with the leaves turning every shade of red and gold. We’ll start by walking along **Broadview Avenue to Pottery Road**, heading down the hill to meet the **Don Valley Trail**. From there, we’ll join the **Crothers Woods Trail**, take in the fall colours, stop for a short break, and then walk back.
There are a few light hills — and one big one at the very end (Pottery Road, I’m looking at you!) — but don’t worry, there’s a sweet reward waiting. After all that hard work, we’ll stop for **Dairy Queen ice cream**! This hike is a bit more challenging than some of our regular walks, but totally worth it for the views (and the ice cream).
**This event happens rain or shine!**
***

item.description:
Beaches Realtor Mark Battenberg invites you to an evening of discovery as he traces the wonderful history of the Upper Beach. From the decline of the great glaciers to the First Nations People, The Kingston Road during the war of 1812, and on to the villages of Norway an Benlamond, which were the cornerstones of the upper Beach, as it grew along The Kings Highway in the mid 1800’s. Discover Coleman’s Corners in Little York, the founding of East Toronto Village, and the rise and fall of the mighty Grand Trunk Railroad. Info: markbattenberg@rogers.com, 647-858-9708

item.title: What is Artificial Intelligence? — Fri Nov 13, 6:00 PM — Scarborough Civic Centre
item.description:
AI technologies have become increasingly prevalent in many aspects of modern life, including healthcare, finance, transportation, and entertainment. Some examples of AI applications include virtual assistants like Siri and Alexa, self-driving cars, fraud detection systems, and personalized recommendations in online shopping. Come join this beginner in-person class to learn what AI is, how it learns and predicts outcomes, considerations when using GenAI applications, and how the Internet of Things (IOT) applies to AI. For ages 13+. Drop-in, no registration required.

Strategies for handling debt, unexpected expenses, and limited income Leveraging campus, community, and financial institution resources Building habits that strengthen financial resilience and confidence
Alumni speaker: Tinotenda Mutsvangwa (BA ’20, MSTM ’21), Financial Advisor at CIBC
Tinotenda is a devoted CIBC Imperial Service Financial Advisor, holding both the (CSC) and (CPH) certifications. With a bachelor’s degree in Political Science and a master’s in Business Management from Schulich School of Business, Tino combines academic excellence with practical expertise to deliver exceptional financial solutions.
